failure_criteria.statement: The dq_check runner returns passed=1, or silently skips, when it cannot actually evaluate a check (e.g. a queried table or column doesn't exist yet, or a fixture is malformed).
failure_criteria.detection: Every checker function has a test asserting it correctly reports passed=0 or raises on an evaluation error -- not only a test asserting it accepts valid input.

failure_criteria.statement: A table/view/row count in this component's code comments, docstrings, or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and its commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: Migration or runner code references ARCHITECTURE.md's DDL block, or a check's expected schema, by an assumption rather than a checked extraction.
failure_criteria.detection: The DDL is parsed from a single well-known fenced block in ARCHITECTURE.md at test time via a shared, tested parser function -- not hand-copied into two places that can silently drift.

failure_criteria.statement: A migration or check-runner error is written to a channel nobody reads (bare print to stdout, a swallowed exception, a log nobody tails).
failure_criteria.detection: Every error path either raises to the caller or is captured in schema_migration.status or dq_check_run.detail in a way a caller/test observes -- never both silent and non-raising.

out_of_scope: Implementing ingest, resolve, snapshot, hookclient, query, or dashboard -- each is a separate component with its own GOALS.json.

Populating or testing against real production data (the live 125,977-row verdict ledger, real TESSERA db, real git repos) -- this component's own tests use synthetic fixtures; end-to-end correctness against real data is foreman:integration-test's job via .foreman/GOALS.integration.json.

Wiring checkers that depend on ingest/resolve's real bookkeeping (e.g. ingest_rows_match_bytes comparing rows_ingested to a real byte range) to real ingest/resolve output -- the checker's own logic and schema-level correctness against injected fixtures is in scope here; real end-to-end wiring is integration-test's job.
Any MAJOR or MINOR architecture-review finding not selected as fix-before-build by the QUALITY-BAR triage -- those are tracked as their own criteria or tickets, not silently folded in here.

amendments.reason: ATLASSN-27 / ATLASSN-29. Forced, not chosen: migrate.apply() raises MigrationError when section 16's DDL hash no longer matches what a database recorded, so a 60-second job calling migrate.connect() against the live version-1 warehouse would trip that raise every 60 seconds. Adding the tables to section 16 instead would force a full re-ingest of 214 MB to gain a table sharing nothing with what is already there. This takes the minimal end of D14 (additive only, no down-migration) and leaves D14 open for the breaking case. Recorded as a provisional decision in DECISION-ATLASSN-27.md.
